messages:
maria: bringing up Hera-7B (open-source fork) on int4. conversion finished but long-context summarization is totally different vs fp16 after ~3k tokens. short snippets look ok. anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

joel: can you paste a minimal repro prompt + output? are you using our usual tokenizer conversion or the model's shipped vocab?

maria: yep. using our convert-tokenmap script (tokmap v2) to map to our tokenizer. repro: feed in a 3.5k-token meeting transcript + "tl;dr" at the end. fp16 -> pretty good. int4 -> repeats, drops sections, and inserts unrelated facts.

maria: example commands:
```bash
python tools/quantize.py --model-dir artifacts/hera_fp16 --out artifacts/hera_int4 --mode int4 --proj-order proj_last --rotary-scale auto
python infra/run_eval.py --model artifacts/hera_int4 --task long_summarize --input tests/long/transcript_3.5k.txt
```

sameer: interesting. can you dump the token ids around where it derails? maybe tokenization or a vocab shift. also dump kvcache head dims shape for first few steps.

maria: dumping now. sample window where it deviates (token ids inline):
```
... 1024 2048 3050 4001 4002 4003 9999 10000 10001 2 17 323 2 ...
```
output fp16 (excerpt): "In summary, the team decided X, action items Y..."
output int4 (excerpt): "The committee adopted Z policy. unrelated company name appears."

anya: could be rotary/headwise scaling mismatch after quant. Did you keep rotary_sin_cos as fp32, or did quantize them? we usually leave sin/cos in fp16 to avoid precision drift for long context.

maria: default quantize.py set rotary params to int8 in this run (we tried to shrink everything). i can re-try leaving sin/cos alone. good call.

joel: also check proj-order: some Gemma->Qwen conversions need proj_first vs proj_last because projection order changes where rotary gets applied. mismatch causes phase misalignment across heads.

sameer: run these quick checks: 1) FP16 model eval on same tokenizer -> baseline. 2) Int4 with rotary params excluded (>fp16) 3) Int4 with --proj-order swapped. compare token-level logit diffs. use tools/logit_diff.py to get per-step KL and argmax changes.

maria: running 1 now. ops-bot: started cluster job 4729 on dedicated-gpu-pool.

ops-bot: Job 4729 queued -> running on gpu-node-14 (NVIDIA A10). ETA ~12m.

maria: quick logit diff after step 512 for int4 (rotary quantized): KL=0.18, argmax changes=4.2% vs fp16; after ~2k tokens KL=1.7, argmax changes=28% -> blowup around that window.

anya: that KL ramp strongly suggests phase drift rather than pure tokenizer issues. check token id parity though as a control. run: 
```bash
python experiments/token_parity.py --model artifacts/hera_fp16 --tok tests/long/transcript_3.5k.txt --dump-ids id_dump_fp16.npy
python experiments/token_parity.py --model artifacts/hera_int4 --tok tests/long/transcript_3.5k.txt --dump-ids id_dump_int4.npy
python tools/compare_ids.py id_dump_fp16.npy id_dump_int4.npy
```

maria: compare_ids shows perfect parity. so tokenization mapping isn't the culprit.

joel: then focus on rotary/kvcache. can you attach a short hex dump of the rotary sin/cos values for both models at init step? like first 8 floats per head.

maria: pasted:
```
fp16 head0 sin: [0.0000, 0.0157, 0.0314, 0.0471, ...]
int4 head0 sin (dequantized): [0.0001, 0.0160, 0.0319, 0.0478, ...]
fp16 head0 cos: [1.0000, 0.9998, 0.9995, 0.9990, ...]
int4 head0 cos (dequantized): [0.9999, 0.9996, 0.9990, 0.9983, ...]
```

sameer: small offsets but shouldn't cause that magnitude of drift unless applied differently per-head. can you dump headwise rotary scale param (some models use headwise scaling factors).

maria: headwise scale present. fp16 headwise_scale[0..3] = [1.0, 0.98, 1.02, 0.99]
int4 dequant headwise_scale = [1.12, 0.87, 0.96, 1.05] -> whoa.

anya: aha. quantization introduced per-head scale distortion. that will change phase alignment across heads and cause long-term drift as phases accumulate with position. probably why short snippets look fine but long contexts diverge.

joel: how did quantize.py handle per-head scales? should be stored in fp16 and not aggressively quantized. Looks like an aggressive symmetric int4 minmax step killed some values. open a PR to change quantize defaults. but first, repro with rotary params preserved.

maria: re-ran with --preserve-rotary-scale and now KL at 2k tokens is 0.34 and argmax changes 5.1% -> much better. summary looks similar to fp16. :relieved:

sameer: great. followups: we need a regression test for long-context rotations in the eval harness. add a test that computes cumulative phase drift (sum of abs difference of sin/cos matrices across positions) and assert below threshold after quantization.

anya: also add an explicit doc in model-onboarding checklist: preserve sin/cos and headwise_scale in fp16, or quantize with per-head calibrated centers. mention proj-order gotcha for Gemma->Qwen conversions.

maria: opened PR #3214 with quantize.py default change + test. linking in case reviewers want to see logs: https://scm.redwood/PR/3214

joel: thumbs up. also note in the conversion notes: if converting from model A to B and head_dim ordering differs, run tools/headmap_inspect.py to ensure projection mapping is consistent. saved us last time.

maria: thanks all. will run expanded int4 sweep tomorrow across longer transcripts and attach results. leaving this thread for now. :+1:
